hypothesis: When growth and inflation are both rising (the leading indicator up over 6 months and y/y inflation up over 3 months), the central bank hikes within 6 months more often than after any month; when both are falling, it cuts within 6 months more often than after any month.
knownLimits: The quadrant is the app's own rule (src/utils/regimeQuadrant.ts): above zero is up on each axis. Only the two matching quadrants make a call; growth up with inflation down, and growth down with inflation up, make none.
The leading indicator and inflation are today's vintages, lagged 1 and 2 months to roughly what was published; revisions are not undone.
Every country with a BIS monthly policy rate, an OECD leading indicator and OECD inflation is pooled; pegs and long holds lower the base rate.
A call is the first month of a run of the same reading; calls in one country are at least a month apart, and runs can be short when the axes sit near zero.
